title: Civil Engineering Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert a civil engineering salary from hourly to annual using the 38-hour week, plus tax, super, and award rates from Fair Work and ABS data.
salarySummary: The median civil engineering salary in Australia is $2,217 per week ($59 per hour) for full-time non-managerial roles, based on ABS data, but your actual annual pay depends on hours worked and applicable awards.

faqs.q: What is the average civil engineering salary in Australia?
faqs.a: According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Survey of Employee Earnings and Hours, May 2025, the median full-time weekly earnings for Civil Engineering Professionals is $2,217, with median hourly earnings of $59. This is well above the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026). However, actual pay varies by experience, location, and whether you are covered by an award or enterprise agreement. Use the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more context.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly civil engineering rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week (the ordinary hours under many awards). For example, $59 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $116,584 per year. If you work 44 hours (the average for civil engineers per ABS), the annual figure would be higher. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site does the maths for you.

faqs.q: Does casual loading apply to civil engineering roles?
faqs.a: Casual loading of 25% applies only if you are employed as a casual under an award that includes it, such as the Professional Employees Award. The National Minimum Wage casual rate is $33.05 per hour (from 1 July 2026). However, many civil engineering professionals are employed full-time or part-time, not casual. If you are casual, use the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page and the checkbox on the timesheet to add the loading on top of your base rate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding your civil engineering salary

When you are offered a civil engineering role, you might see an hourly rate or an annual salary figure. To compare offers or plan your budget, you need to convert between the two. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume 38 hours per week for a full-time role, because that is the ordinary hours used in most awards and the National Minimum Wage calculation. However, civil engineering professionals often work more. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) data cited by, the average full-time hours for this occupation is 44 hours per week. The median weekly earnings are $2,217, which gives a median hourly rate of $59.

If you are paid $59 per hour and work 38 hours, your annual pay would be $59 × 38 × 52 = $116,584. If you work 44 hours, it would be $59 × 44 × 52 = $134,992. The fortnightly equivalent is weekly pay multiplied by two: $2,217 × 2 = $4,434 before tax.

### Distinguishing minimum wage, award rates, and market rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This is the legal floor. Most civil engineering professionals earn much more, but your specific award or enterprise agreement may set minimum rates. The Professional Employees Award, for example, covers many engineers. Award rates include penalty rates, allowances, and casual loading (25% on top for casuals). The median civil engineering salary of $2,217 per week is a market figure, not an award minimum.

## Tax and super on your civil engineering salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate tax and super. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (single rate, no reduction assumed here). For a gross annual salary of $116,584, the estimated tax would be approximately $26,000–$27,000, leaving a take-home pay of around $89,000–$90,000. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for a detailed calculator.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your pay. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per quarter (2026–27). For a $116,584 salary, super would be about $13,990 per year, added to your super fund. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

### Fortnightly and weekly breakdown

If you are paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the median weekly earnings of $2,217, your fortnightly gross would be $4,434. After tax and Medicare, a single person might take home roughly $3,500–$3,600 per fortnight, depending on your exact tax situation.

## Using the timesheet tool

This site’s [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading with a checkbox. It then calculates annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures, plus estimated tax and super. Remember: the annual figure is hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is an estimate, not a guarantee.

For award-specific rates, check the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. For more on minimum wage and casual loading, see [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading). The [reference tables](/data) have historical rates.

### Important note on the estimate

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Civil engineering salary in context

Comparing your offer to the median civil engineering salary of $2,217 per week gives you a benchmark. If your hourly rate is below $59, you may be below the median; if above, you are above. Remember that the median is for full-time non-managerial employees and excludes part-time and junior roles. The [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page has more occupation-specific data.

Whether you are negotiating a new role or checking your current pay, understanding the conversion from hourly to annual helps you make informed decisions. Use the tools on this site to run the numbers for your specific situation.
